description: Web dashboard served by the Creel daemon for managing tasks, cron jobs, workspace files, and config. React + TypeScript + MUI v6 + Vite frontend, FastAPI backend.

userStories.title: Static SPA serving from FastAPI daemon
userStories.description: The daemon should serve the built React app as static files so visiting localhost:8099 loads the dashboard.
acceptanceCriteria: FastAPI daemon mounts StaticFiles at '/' serving built React app from src/taskrunner/dashboard_static/
index.html is served for all non-API routes (SPA fallback) so client-side routing works
API routes remain at /v1/... (existing) and /api/... (new dashboard endpoints)
When dashboard_static/ directory is missing or empty, the daemon starts normally without errors
Existing /health and /v1/* endpoints still work unchanged
Typecheck passes, existing tests pass
userStories.notes: Modify src/taskrunner/daemon/api.py. Use FastAPI StaticFiles mount. SPA fallback: catch-all route that returns index.html for non-API paths.

userStories.title: Vite + React + TypeScript scaffold
userStories.description: Create the frontend project skeleton with Vite, React 18+, and TypeScript.
acceptanceCriteria: dashboard/ directory contains a working Vite + React 18 + TypeScript project
npm install && npm run build produces output in dashboard/dist/
A build script scripts/build-dashboard.sh copies dashboard/dist/ to src/taskrunner/dashboard_static/
dashboard/src/main.tsx renders <App /> into #root
TypeScript strict mode enabled in tsconfig.json
Vite dev server proxies /api/* and /v1/* to localhost:8099 for local development
.gitignore includes dashboard/node_modules/, dashboard/dist/, src/taskrunner/dashboard_static/
userStories.notes: Use npm create vite@latest with react-ts template. Keep it minimal — just the scaffold.

userStories.title: Material UI setup and theming
userStories.description: Install and configure MUI v6 with dark mode support.
acceptanceCriteria: MUI installed: @mui/material, @mui/icons-material, @emotion/react, @emotion/styled
MUI ThemeProvider wraps the app with createTheme()
Dark mode toggle in header, persisted to localStorage
MUI theme palette defines the color scheme
App renders without console errors in both light and dark mode
userStories.notes: Use MUI's built-in dark mode via palette.mode. Store preference in localStorage key 'creel-theme'.

userStories.title: Layout shell with sidebar and routing
userStories.description: Create the main layout with collapsible sidebar navigation and React Router.
acceptanceCriteria: React Router v6 with routes: /, /tasks, /tasks/:name, /tasks/new, /cron, /files, /config, /logs
Persistent MUI Drawer sidebar with nav links grouped: Control (Overview, Tasks, Cron Jobs), Workspace (Files, Config), System (Logs)
Active page highlighted in sidebar using MUI ListItemButton selected state
Header AppBar with: Creel name, daemon connection status badge (green/red Chip), dark mode toggle IconButton
Sidebar collapses on screens < 768px (MUI responsive Drawer — temporary variant on mobile)
404 page for unknown routes
Each route renders a placeholder page component with the page title
userStories.notes: Use MUI Drawer (permanent on desktop, temporary on mobile), AppBar, List, ListItemButton, ListItemIcon, ListItemText. Use react-router-dom NavLink for active state.

userStories.title: Status API endpoint
userStories.description: Backend endpoint that returns daemon status, agent info, and summary stats for the overview page.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/status returns JSON with: daemon (running, pid, uptime_seconds, socket), agent (name, model, provider), channels list with enabled/connected status, tasks (total, scheduled counts), cron (enabled_jobs, total_jobs, next_run), recent_runs (last 5 with task name, status, finished_at, duration_ms)
Endpoint reads agent config from agent.yaml via existing config loading
Endpoint reads task files from tasks directory
Returns sensible defaults when no tasks/channels exist
Existing tests still pass
userStories.notes: Create src/taskrunner/daemon/api_dashboard.py with an APIRouter. Mount it in api.py. Use existing model loading and service status methods where possible.

userStories.title: Overview page with live status
userStories.description: Frontend overview page that displays daemon status, agent info, channel health, and recent activity.
acceptanceCriteria: Overview page fetches GET /api/status on mount and displays data in MUI Card components
Daemon status card: running/stopped badge, PID, uptime (human readable), socket path
Agent info card: name, model, provider
Channels section: list of channels with green/red Chip badges for connected/disconnected
Quick stats: total tasks, scheduled tasks, enabled cron jobs, next scheduled run
Recent runs: MUI Table with last 5 runs showing task name, status Chip (success=green, failed=red, timeout=orange), finished time (relative), duration
Auto-refreshes every 30 seconds via polling
Loading skeleton shown while fetching
Error state shown if daemon is unreachable
userStories.notes: Use MUI Card, CardContent, Chip, Table, Skeleton. Create dashboard/src/api/client.ts with a fetch wrapper.

userStories.title: Task CRUD API endpoints
userStories.description: Backend REST API for listing, reading, creating, updating, and deleting task definitions.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/tasks returns list of all tasks from tasks directory: name, description, schedule, enabled, last_modified, file_path
GET /api/tasks/{name} returns full task as JSON plus raw_yaml field with file contents
POST /api/tasks creates new task YAML file — validates with Pydantic, returns 409 if exists
PUT /api/tasks/{name} updates existing task — creates .bak backup before overwriting, validates, returns 404 if not found
DELETE /api/tasks/{name} moves file to .deleted/ subdirectory (not permanent delete), returns 404 if not found
POST /api/tasks/{name}/run triggers run_task() in background thread, returns 202 with run_id
All endpoints return consistent error JSON: {error, detail}
Existing tests still pass
userStories.notes: Create src/taskrunner/daemon/api_tasks.py with APIRouter. Use existing models.load_all_tasks() and orchestrator.run_task(). Task files live in the configured tasks directory.

userStories.title: Task list page
userStories.description: Frontend page showing all tasks in a table with search, sort, and enable/disable toggles.
acceptanceCriteria: MUI Table with columns: Name, Description, Schedule (human-readable), Last Modified, Enabled (Switch toggle)
Enabled toggle calls PUT /api/tasks/{name} to flip enabled field
TextField search input filters tasks by name/description (client-side)
Column headers clickable to sort by name, schedule, last modified
New Task button (MUI Button with AddIcon) in top-right, navigates to /tasks/new
Click task name navigates to /tasks/{name}
Empty state: 'No tasks yet. Create your first task.' with button
Loading skeleton while fetching
userStories.notes: Use MUI Table, TableHead, TableBody, TableRow, TableCell, TableSortLabel, Switch, TextField, Button.

userStories.title: Task edit and create page
userStories.description: Form for creating and editing tasks with both form fields and raw YAML editing.
acceptanceCriteria: Form mode with MUI fields: Name (TextField, required, slug pattern [a-z0-9-]), Description (TextField multiline), Schedule (TextField with human-readable preview below), Prompt (TextField multiline, required), Model override (TextField, optional), Timeout (TextField type=number), Output type (Select: stdout/imessage/file), Output target (TextField), Enabled (Checkbox)
Raw YAML tab with CodeMirror 6 editor: YAML syntax highlighting, line numbers
MUI Tabs component to switch between Form and Raw modes
Switching tabs syncs content (form changes reflected in raw YAML and vice versa)
Save button calls POST (create) or PUT (edit) API — shows Snackbar success toast
Save disabled when no changes (dirty tracking)
Run Now button (edit mode only) triggers POST /api/tasks/{name}/run
Delete button (edit mode only) with Dialog confirmation
Form validation: required fields show error state, slug pattern validated on name
Unsaved changes warning via beforeunload event
Schedule preset helper: Select dropdown with common schedules (hourly, daily 9am, weekly Monday) that fills the cron field
userStories.notes: Install @codemirror/lang-yaml, @codemirror/view, @codemirror/state. Use js-yaml for YAML<->JSON conversion in the browser. Handle form<->raw sync carefully — only sync on tab switch, not on every keystroke.

userStories.title: Cron history storage
userStories.description: The scheduler should persist cron run history to a JSONL file for the dashboard to display.
acceptanceCriteria: After each scheduled task execution, a record is appended to ~/.creel/cron-history.jsonl
Record format: {run_id, job_name, started_at, finished_at, duration_ms, status (success/failed/timeout), token_usage, error, summary}
run_id is a UUID4
Error field contains traceback string on failure, null on success
Summary field contains truncated response text (first 500 chars)
File is created automatically if it doesn't exist
Existing scheduler tests still pass
userStories.notes: Modify src/taskrunner/scheduler.py _run_task_safe() to write records. Use json.dumps() + file append. Import uuid for run_id generation.

userStories.title: Cron API endpoints
userStories.description: Backend API for listing cron jobs, toggling them, and querying run history.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/cron/jobs returns tasks with schedule field set: name, schedule, schedule_human (readable), next_run, last_run, last_status, enabled
POST /api/cron/jobs/{name}/toggle enables/disables job — updates YAML enabled field
GET /api/cron/history returns paginated run history from cron-history.jsonl: query params ?job=name&status=success|failed|timeout&limit=50&offset=0
GET /api/cron/history/{run_id} returns full detail of a single run
schedule_human converts cron expressions to readable strings (e.g., '0 9 * * *' -> 'Every day at 9:00 AM')
Returns empty lists gracefully when no history exists
Existing tests still pass
userStories.notes: Create src/taskrunner/daemon/api_cron.py. For cron-to-human conversion, use a simple mapping or cronstrue library. Read JSONL file with line-by-line JSON parsing.

userStories.title: Cron jobs page
userStories.description: Frontend page with job list, run history, and new job creation form.
acceptanceCriteria: Job list panel: MUI Table with Name, Schedule, Next Run, Last Run, Status (Chip), Enabled (Switch toggle)
Sort by next run (default), name — via TableSortLabel
Filter dropdown: All/Enabled/Disabled
Search by name (TextField)
Click a job to filter run history below to that job
Run history panel: MUI Table with Job Name, Started, Duration, Status Chip, Summary (truncated)
Filter by status: toggle ButtonGroup (All/Success/Failed/Timeout)
Click history row to expand (MUI Collapse) showing full details: prompt, response, tokens, error
Pagination: 'Load more' button at bottom, default 50 rows

New Job dialog (MUI Dialog): name, schedule type (Select: 'Every X' or 'Cron expression'), interval fields or cron input with human preview, prompt (TextField multiline), model override, timeout, enabled checkbox, Create button
Empty states for both panels
userStories.notes: Split into two panels using MUI Grid or Stack. Use Collapse for expandable rows. Dialog for new job form.

userStories.title: File browser API endpoints
userStories.description: Backend API for browsing and editing files in ~/.creel/.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/files/tree returns recursive directory tree of ~/.creel/: name, path, type (file/dir), size_bytes, modified_at, children
Excludes: __pycache__, .pyc, daemon.sock, daemon.pid, *.bak, .git, .deleted
Max depth: 5 levels
GET /api/files/{path} returns file contents: path, content, size_bytes, modified_at — returns binary:true for non-text files
Max file size for content: 1MB, returns error for larger
PUT /api/files/{path} writes file — creates .bak backup, creates parent dirs if needed
POST /api/files/{path} creates new file — returns 409 if exists
DELETE /api/files/{path} moves to .trash/ — returns 400 for protected files (agent.yaml, daemon.pid, daemon.sock)
ALL paths validated to be within ~/.creel/ — reject any ../ traversal with 400
Existing tests still pass
userStories.notes: Create src/taskrunner/daemon/api_files.py. Use pathlib for path resolution and security validation. Resolve symlinks before checking containment.

userStories.title: File browser page
userStories.description: Frontend with tree navigation and CodeMirror code editor for browsing and editing workspace files.
acceptanceCriteria: Left panel: MUI TreeView with expandable directory tree, file icons by extension (using MUI icons: Description for .yaml, Article for .md, DataObject for .json, Folder for dirs)
Quick Access section pinned at top with: agent.yaml, workspace/SOUL.md, workspace/USER.md, workspace/MEMORY.md
Click file opens in right panel editor
Right panel: CodeMirror 6 with auto-detected language mode (YAML, Markdown, JSON, plain text based on extension)
Line numbers, active line highlighting, bracket matching enabled
Breadcrumb above editor showing current file path
Save button (and Ctrl/Cmd+S keyboard shortcut) writes via PUT API — Snackbar confirmation
Unsaved changes dot indicator next to filename
For .md files: toggle IconButton to switch Edit vs Preview (rendered with a markdown-to-html library)
New File dialog: TextField for path, Select for template (blank, YAML task, Markdown note)
Empty state when no file selected: 'Select a file from the tree to edit'
userStories.notes: Use MUI TreeView from @mui/x-tree-view. Install @codemirror/lang-json, @codemirror/lang-markdown in addition to yaml. For markdown preview, use react-markdown or marked.

userStories.title: Config API endpoints
userStories.description: Backend API for reading and writing agent.yaml configuration.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/config returns parsed agent.yaml as JSON plus raw_yaml field
PUT /api/config accepts {json: {...}} or {raw_yaml: '...'} — validates against AgentConfig model, creates .bak backup, returns 400 with validation errors if invalid
POST /api/config/apply performs graceful daemon restart to pick up changes — returns 202
GET /api/config/schema returns JSON Schema derived from AgentConfig Pydantic model (using model_json_schema())
Existing tests still pass
userStories.notes: Create src/taskrunner/daemon/api_config.py. For restart: signal the daemon to re-read config and restart the scheduler. Use Pydantic model_json_schema() for schema generation.

userStories.title: Config editor page
userStories.description: Frontend config editor with form mode and raw YAML mode.
acceptanceCriteria: MUI Tabs: Form | Raw

Form mode with collapsible MUI Accordion sections: Agent (name, model, provider, max_tokens), Channels (per-channel sub-accordions with relevant fields), Guardian (enabled Switch, policy path), Daemon (log level Select, port TextField), Tools (list of tool configs)
Field types rendered appropriately: TextField, Select, Switch, TextField type=number
Help text below fields (MUI FormHelperText) from schema descriptions
Validation errors shown inline (TextField error prop + helperText)
Raw mode: full CodeMirror YAML editor
Switching tabs syncs content
Save button writes to disk — Snackbar toast
Apply button saves AND triggers POST /api/config/apply with Dialog confirmation: 'This will restart the daemon. Active sessions will be interrupted.'
Unsaved changes Chip badge next to save button showing change count
userStories.notes: Dynamically generate form from JSON Schema where possible. Fall back to TextField for unknown field types. Use MUI Accordion, AccordionSummary, AccordionDetails for sections.

userStories.title: Log streaming API
userStories.description: WebSocket endpoint for streaming daemon logs to the dashboard.
acceptanceCriteria: WebSocket endpoint at /ws/logs streams daemon log lines as JSON: {timestamp, level, module, message}
Reads from ~/.creel/daemon.log tail plus new lines as they're written
Client can send filter messages: {level: 'WARN'} to filter server-side
GET /api/logs/recent?limit=200&level=INFO returns recent lines as non-streaming fallback
WebSocket handles client disconnects gracefully
Existing tests still pass
userStories.notes: Use FastAPI WebSocket support. Use asyncio file watching or periodic tail for new lines. Parse log lines into structured JSON.

userStories.title: Logs page with live streaming
userStories.description: Frontend log viewer with live updates, level filtering, and search.
acceptanceCriteria: Live-updating log display using WebSocket connection to /ws/logs
Level filter: MUI ToggleButtonGroup with ALL, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR (multi-select)
TextField search to filter log lines by text (client-side)
Pause Button to stop auto-scroll — shows Chip with 'N new lines' count
Click chip or unpause jumps to bottom
Each log line shows: timestamp, level (color-coded Chip — blue=DEBUG, green=INFO, orange=WARN, red=ERROR), module, message
Download log Button triggers file download of full daemon.log
Max 1000 lines in view — older lines discarded as new arrive
Graceful WebSocket reconnect with 'Reconnecting...' Alert banner
Falls back to polling GET /api/logs/recent if WebSocket fails
userStories.notes: Use MUI ToggleButtonGroup, Chip, Alert. Virtualized list (react-window or similar) for performance with 1000 lines. Auto-reconnect with exponential backoff.

userStories.title: API authentication
userStories.description: Protect all dashboard API endpoints with token auth.
acceptanceCriteria: All /api/* endpoints require Authorization: Bearer <token> header or ?token=<token> query param
Token stored in ~/.creel/dashboard-token (auto-generated UUID on first daemon start if missing)
Unauthenticated requests return 401 JSON: {error: 'unauthorized'}
Dashboard frontend stores token in localStorage after entry in a login dialog
Login dialog shown on 401 response — TextField for token, Submit button
/health endpoint remains unauthenticated
Existing /v1/* endpoints remain unchanged (backward compat)
userStories.notes: Use FastAPI Depends() with a token checker for /api/* routes. Generate token with uuid4 on first start. Frontend: intercept 401 in fetch wrapper and show login dialog.

userStories.title: Build script and packaging
userStories.description: Build pipeline that bundles the frontend into the Python wheel.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/build-dashboard.sh runs: cd dashboard && npm ci && npm run build, then copies dist/ to src/taskrunner/dashboard_static/
pyproject.toml includes dashboard_static/ as package data via force-include
.gitignore includes dashboard/node_modules/, dashboard/dist/, src/taskrunner/dashboard_static/
Dashboard loads with no external CDN/network requests (all assets bundled)
pip install . from repo root includes the dashboard and it loads at localhost:8099/
Build script is idempotent and handles missing node_modules gracefully
dashboard/README.md documents: npm install, npm run dev, npm run build
userStories.notes: Add to pyproject.toml: [tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include] 'src/taskrunner/dashboard_static' = 'taskrunner/dashboard_static'. Vite build should produce minimal output with no external fetches.
